name: Language Failover
description: Per-user audio and subtitle language priority with fallback. Automatically selects the best audio and subtitle tracks based on an ordered language preference list, with per-series overrides.
overview: Multi-language fallback for audio and subtitles

versions.changelog:
Support for **Jellyfin 12.x**. This release does not run on Jellyfin 10.11 — see below.

## ⬆️ Upgrading

**This version requires Jellyfin Server 12.0 or later.** Jellyfin 12.0 moved the server to
.NET 10 and broke the plugin ABI, so the plugin had to be rebuilt against it.

- **On Jellyfin 12.x** — straight upgrade from 1.2.0.1. No configuration changes; your
  per-user language lists and per-series overrides carry over untouched.
- **Still on Jellyfin 10.11?** Nothing to do, and nothing will break. The catalogue filters
  versions by `targetAbi`, so a 10.11 server never sees 1.3.0.0 and will neither offer nor
  install it; your 1.2.0.1 keeps working exactly as it does today. The 10.11 line is no
  longer maintained, so upgrading the server is the way to get future fixes.

After upgrading the **server** to 12.0, run a full library scan before judging the plugin:
the 12.0 migration drops auto-resolved alternate versions, and until the scan restores them
the plugin has no media streams to choose from on those titles.

## 🔧 Under the hood

- **Retargeted to .NET 10**, built against the Jellyfin 12.0 SDK — `Jellyfin.Controller` and
  `Jellyfin.Model` at 12.0.0 rather than 12.1.0, so the build stays loadable on a 12.0 server;
  nothing the plugin uses was added in 12.1.
- **`targetAbi` raised to 12.0.0.0.** This is the single line that keeps the release invisible
  to 10.11 servers, and it is why nothing breaks for anyone who has not upgraded.
- The build and release workflows move to the .NET 10 SDK, and the release job packages from
  `bin/Release/net10.0`.
- Test tooling moved with the target framework: `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` 17.11.1 → 18.10.1 and
  `xunit.runner.visualstudio` 2.8.2 → 3.1.5, both of which predate .NET 10 and cannot run a
  `net10.0` test assembly.
- **No plugin code changed.** Every server API the selection logic touches is unchanged in
  12.x — the playback-start event and its arguments, media stream lookup, the track-selection
  commands, and ISO 639 language resolution. Track selection behaves exactly as in 1.2.0.1.
- The only source changes are in the test project. The `ILocalizationManager` fake grew the
  two members 12.x added to that interface (`GetServerLocalizedString`,
  `GetLanguageDisplayName`), and the catalogue checks were rewritten: the old one required
  every entry to carry the same `targetAbi`, which stopped being true the moment the catalogue
  started serving two ABI lines. Two rules replace it — an entry may never declare a newer ABI
  than the build, and a newer version may never declare an older ABI than an existing entry,
  which is what would make a 12.x server download the 10.11 build.

A patch for 1.2.0.0: the language dropdowns on the configuration page were unreadable.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Dropdown lists were white-on-white.** On a dark Jellyfin theme, opening the user picker or any language selector showed a light popup with white text — every entry invisible except the one under the cursor. The popup is drawn by the browser in its own light/dark scheme, while the text colour was still being taken from the Jellyfin theme; the two are now read as a pair so they can never disagree. The series search results panel had the same latent problem and was fixed with it.

## 🔧 Under the hood

- The release workflow now refuses to publish from a tag with no release note, instead of silently falling back to the last commit message. That fallback is why **1.2.0.0 appears in the catalogue as *"Merge branch 'develop'"*** — its real release notes are on the [GitHub releases page](https://github.com/Hightmar/jellyfin-langage-failover/releases).

## ⬆️ Upgrading

Straight upgrade from 1.2.0.0 — no configuration changes. If you are coming from 1.1.x, read the 1.2.0.0 notes first: subtitle selection changed there. Server compatibility is unchanged (**Jellyfin 10.11.x**).
